evals.name: code-over-stale-prose
evals.prompt: Review documentation: Parse returns ErrEmpty only for an empty string, but its comment promises ErrEmpty for whitespace too. Tests confirm whitespace is valid. No intent or design record is supplied.

assertions.text: Identifies the mismatch using supplied implementation and tests.
Does not invent intent or change implementation to satisfy stale prose.

evals.name: version-floor
evals.prompt: Update Go setup docs. go.mod says go 1.22; CI supports 1.22 and 1.24. The local toolchain is 1.24. A draft says go get -tool installs our doc generator.

assertions.text: Checks command compatibility with Go 1.22 and avoids treating local 1.24 as the support floor.
Uses a compatible verified installation approach or reports missing tooling evidence; does not raise go.mod.

evals.name: configuration-precedence
evals.prompt: Write configuration docs from this Go loader: start with defaults, apply config file, apply explicitly set flags, then apply nonempty APP_PORT env. File and env ports are decimal integers. Default is 8080.

assertions.text: States environment overrides explicit flags in this loader.
Documents default and integer format without adding unsupported configuration sources.

evals.name: example-association
evals.prompt: In a Go package client exporting New and (*Client).Get, explain executable example names for construction, Get, and a cached variant.

assertions.text: Uses ExampleNew, ExampleClient_Get, and ExampleClient_Get_cached.
Explains _test.go placement and prefers external package client_test for public usage.

evals.name: compile-vs-execute
evals.prompt: Review these Go documentation checks: ExampleNew has no output comment; README has a Go code fence; go test -run ExampleMissing reports no tests to run. The author says all examples passed.

assertions.text: Distinguishes compiled ExampleNew from executed output checks.
Does not treat README fences or an empty test selection as tested examples.

evals.name: output-contract
evals.prompt: A Go Example prints two identical lines named ready. Expected output uses Unordered output with only one ready line. Another Example has an empty Output directive. Explain execution semantics.

assertions.text: Says unordered output still checks duplicate counts.
Says empty Output executes and asserts empty stdout.

evals.name: deprecation-evidence
evals.prompt: Write a doc comment for deprecated Go Parse in favor of ParseStrict. No removal release or date has been decided.

assertions.text: Uses Deprecated: in its own paragraph with the supplied replacement.
Invents no removal deadline or release.

evals.name: release-scope
evals.prompt: Write Go changelog text for this supplied change: decoder now rejects a negative length before allocating. No performance measurements, release date, or security assessment exist.

assertions.text: States the specific observable fix.
Does not invent performance gains, broad reliability claims, release dates, or security conclusions.

evals.name: generator-version
evals.prompt: Review Go API documentation saying our pinned Swagger 2 generator emits OpenAPI 3 and requiring go get -tool on a Go 1.22 project.

assertions.text: Flags both format and toolchain incompatibilities.
Requires checking pinned generator configuration instead of changing dependencies or generated output alone.

evals.name: private-docs
evals.prompt: Improve a private Go library README and package docs. The old checklist mandates public Playground links and registration on documentation aggregators.

assertions.text: Keeps private documentation local unless public sharing is authorized.
Does not fabricate URLs or perform external registration.

evals.name: installation-evidence
evals.prompt: Write install docs for a Go repo example.com/acme/tool/v2 with command at cmd/tool, go 1.23, no release assets, and no Homebrew or container distribution.

assertions.text: Uses the actual versioned command path for source installation.
Does not invent binary downloads, package managers, or images.

evals.name: practical-verification
evals.prompt: Update a Go README example against the current local API. A previous run compiled it against a published version instead. The minimum supported toolchain is unavailable.

assertions.text: Checks the snippet against the local module rather than accidentally using the published version.
Reports which toolchain ran and leaves minimum-version execution unverified.
